text: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan led a $5 billion bond sale for Oracle, and JPMorgan provided a $2 billion bridge loan to fund the acquisition.
Apple shares rose 5% after the company reported quarterly earnings that beat analyst estimates.
The local bakery opened a second location downtown, offering sourdough and pastries to weekend crowds.
The Federal Reserve left its overnight reverse repo rate unchanged and signaled it would keep policy steady through year-end.
Airbus received orders for 50 A320neo jets from IndiGo, lifting its backlog to a record as airlines expand fleets.
Manchester United beat Liverpool 2-1 at Old Trafford on Sunday, with a late goal from the captain.
Treasury 10-year yields climbed to 4.2% after stronger-than-expected payrolls data reduced bets on rate cuts.
Primary dealers bought 45% of the $40 billion 10-year note auction, and banks' rates desks reported heavy client demand for swaptions.
Citigroup's FX desk handled record client volumes in yen forwards as exporters rushed to hedge ahead of the Bank of Japan meeting.
The euro fell 0.8% against the dollar after weaker German factory data.
A dealer structured an equity derivative for institutional investors tied to Apple shares, hedging its exposure through the cash market.
Morgan Stanley sold a $1.2 billion block of Uber shares overnight to institutional investors at a 3% discount.
Barclays and HSBC are bookrunners on Rivian's $2 billion initial public offering, which priced at the top of the range.
Ford sold $3 billion of bonds on Tuesday, its largest debt offering in two years, according to a company filing.
JPMorgan's repo desk extended $10 billion of reverse repo financing to hedge-fund clients against Treasury collateral as basis trades grew.
Goldman Sachs's prime brokerage unit cut financing to several hedge funds after margin calls on concentrated stock positions.
Deutsche Bank priced a $600 million CLO backed by leveraged loans, with the AAA tranche sold to Japanese investors.
Credit-default swaps on Italian banks widened to the highest level in a year, signaling rising perceived risk.
Banks posted large CVA losses on uncollateralised swaps with energy companies as counterparty credit spreads surged.
Bank of America and Wells Fargo provided a $4 billion five-year revolving credit facility to Procter & Gamble for general corporate purposes.
KKR's buyout of a software maker is backed by $3.5 billion of leveraged loans arranged by Credit Suisse and Barclays.
Lenders including MUFG and SMBC signed a $1.8 billion non-recourse loan for an offshore wind farm, to be repaid from the project's power sales.
BNP Paribas financed the delivery of four Boeing 787s to Air France through a secured loan backed by the aircraft.
UK banks approved 65,000 mortgages for house purchase in March as first-time buyers returned to the market.
US home prices rose 6% from a year earlier, according to the Case-Shiller index.
Lloyds expanded its lending to small businesses under a government-backed loan scheme, approving 20,000 loans to firms with fewer than 50 staff.
Standard Chartered issued $300 million of letters of credit to support commodity imports by Indian refiners.
Capital One said credit-card charge-offs rose to 5.1% as consumers struggled with higher borrowing costs.
Blackstone's latest private-equity fund secured a $2 billion subscription credit line from a group of banks led by Wells Fargo.
UBS sold $3 billion of its own senior bonds to refinance maturing debt and bolster its funding ahead of new regulatory requirements.
HSBC increased its holdings of high-quality liquid assets, lifting its liquidity coverage ratio to 140%.
Wells Fargo added interest-rate swaps to hedge its fixed-rate securities portfolio, protecting net interest income from rising rates.
